$comment: Phase 787 — the pinned prover for every model under proofs/ (RemotingDecode.fst, and since Phase 790 DisclosureFold.fst; check.ps1 carries the module list).
F* releases WEEKLY (five releases in the four weeks to 2026-09-13), and a proof is a
claim about a specific prover: an unpinned toolchain would silently change what the
green tick means, and proof hints no longer exist to stabilise it (--record_hints and
--use_hints were removed from F*), so reproducibility rests on this pin, on --quake,
and on the margin in z3rlimit. The release bundles Z3, so the pin covers the solver too
— three of them, and z3version names which one is used.
The hash is over the downloaded archive; proofs/check.ps1 verifies it before extracting
and refuses to proceed on a mismatch.
Phase 792 adds ModelInput.fst, the model-input admissibility theorem. It needed no flag
change either: the `extract` set below still carries only --codegen FSharp, and check.ps1
appends --extract <module> per entry of its own module list. A model that ever DID need a
flag of its own would take a per-module override here rather than widening this set.
Phase 795 appended TaintFlow.fst to check.ps1's module list and needed no flag change here:
the shared check/extract/quake sets already cover it, and its extraction references the same
five Prims names the shim already carries. A module needing its own flags would be the first.
Phase 788 appended ElmishRing.fst and ElmishSub.fst — the Elmish runtime's ring buffer and
subscription diff — and needed no flag change either. ElmishRing.fst is the first model to cite
a ulib lemma (FStar.Math.Lemmas, in the ghost `succ_is_mod` only, so the extraction is unchanged);
the release ships ulib's checked files, so the cold check still needs nothing beyond the pin.
Phase 789 appended ElmishLoop.fst — the dispatch loop as a step machine — with no flag change. It is
the first module to open another (ElmishRing); the check's per-run cache is what resolves that, so
check.ps1's list order (ElmishRing before ElmishLoop) is load-bearing rather than the pin.
Phase 955 moved the pin from v2026.09.06 to v2026.09.27 with no flag change: all eight models check
on it over three cold runs with --quake 3, and every extraction through `--codegen FSharp` is
byte-identical to the one the old pin produced. The release still bundles Z3 4.13.3. What the move
is FOR is the second extraction pipeline this release carries (`--codegen Custard`, with an F#
backend) and the Pulse library it ships under lib/fstar/pulse; proofs/README.md records what was
measured on both. Upstream describes `--codegen FSharp` as unmaintained, so the `extract` set below
names a route that is kept working by this repository's normaliser rather than by the prover.
Phase 955 also appended ElmishRingArray.fst, the first Pulse module and the first extracted through
that second pipeline: the `custard` set below is its route, and check.ps1 appends one
`--custard_entry <definition>` per root the module's entry names and the `-o` path. The Pulse
library is on the prover's own include path (lib/fstar/fstar.include), so the check set is unchanged.
Phase 957 moved the pin from v2026.09.27 to v2026.10.11, the first weekly release carrying the two Custard
fixes Phase 955 reported (FStarLang/FStar#4626 and #4627, both ancestors of the release tag by commit
ancestry; there was no release between 09.27 and 10.11). The move is not optional in the way the earlier
ones were: upstream #4653 (merged 2026-10-10) made Custard the only extraction backend, so this release has
no `--codegen Custard`, no `--custard_backend`, no `--extract` and no legacy F# printer — `--codegen FSharp`
now names Custard's F# backend. The `extract` set below is therefore the one route for all nine modules, and
the `custard` set that named the second route is gone with the first. The release still bundles Z3 4.13.3.
The leg could not run the legacy route on this release first, as 957.A asked, because the route does not
exist on it; the last green legacy run is Phase 955's on v2026.09.27, recorded in proofs/README.md.

linux-x64.$comment: Declared but NOT hash-pinned: nothing in this repo has run the proof leg on Linux, and an unverified hash recorded as if it were verified is worse than an absent one. check.ps1 refuses a platform whose sha256 is empty and says why. The CI job runs windows-latest for this reason.

flags.$comment: --z3rlimit 60 against modules whose slowest query finishes well inside the default is a deliberate MARGIN, not a requirement: with hints gone, the thing that makes a check flaky is a query landing near the limit on a slower machine, and headroom is the cheapest defence available. `extract` is the ONE route (Phase 957): Custard's F# backend, which on this release is what `--codegen FSharp` names, run once over the whole program with every module a root — check.ps1 appends one `--custard_entry_module <module>` per entry of its list and every source file, and `--ext fly_deps=0` is what lets one invocation take more than one file. `--custard_split` writes one F# module per F* module under its own name, so a cross-module reference is `ElmishRing.push` rather than a mangled global. There is no second set: the legacy printer, its `--extract` option and `--custard_backend` were all removed upstream before this release.
